# Frozen-model deployment: October and November 2026

The already-trained Meridian models were loaded from their saved weights (sha256-checked), **not trained, fine-tuned or recalibrated**, and run forward on market data that arrived after their training period. Every comparison model was fit once on data ending at the same cut-off and then also run forward frozen. Target: next-day Garman–Klass realized variance; loss: QLIKE (lower is better). Reference: per-asset HAR-RV. Pipeline: `scripts/deploy_data.py` → `scripts/deploy_frozen.py` → `scripts/score_deploy.py`; independent checks: `scripts/audit_deploy.py` (results in `results/deploy/audit_report.md`).

## What is the WM component, and what could be deployed

**Meridian-WM** (`meridian/meridian_wm.py`, class `MeridianWM`) is the bridged world-model network: (1) a sticky switching-SSM belief core (`meridian/switching.py`, K=3 soft regimes, posterior α_t, regime = argmax α_t) with its own QLIKE head; (2) a decoupled plain diagonal-SSM volatility core with an EMA target encoder whose smoothed belief feeds the point log-variance head (QLIKE); (3) a small Student-t head over next-day returns (tail heaviness and scale) reading the stop-gradient belief; (4) a JEPA predictor + SIGReg auxiliary loss whose latent prediction error is the surprise score. The wider *world model* (`WORLD_MODEL.md`, `scripts/world_model.py`) is a bank of separately trained modules (volatility, tail, regime, factor, connectedness, propagation, covariance) linked by inspectable combiners into `results/world_state.json`.

**No trained `MeridianWM` weights exist in the repository**: `scripts/run_wm.py`, `scripts/live.py` and `scripts/world_model.py` train it from scratch on every run and never save it. Deploying it would require training, so it is not deployed here. Its pre-audit numbers stay withdrawn (`WORLD_MODEL.md`). What *is* saved, and is deployed below without any training, is the world model's **volatility module** in two frozen snapshots:

- **Snapshot A** — `results/forward/frozen/` Meridian M0 (the audited configuration: SSM belief core, HAR-anchored, QLIKE-trained, 5 seeds), trained on labels through 2026-10-30. October 2026 is inside its training data, so only November 2026 is scored for it.
- **Snapshot B** — `results/meridian_final.pt`, the pre-audit single-seed Meridian (11 inputs, MSE head = E[log RV]). Its cut-off was not recorded; audit check T4 reconstructs it from the saved feature scaler: it was trained on the *uncleaned* pre-audit bars with origins through late July 2026. October and November 2026 are therefore more than two months out of sample. Its comparison models were fit through 2026-09-08 (the file's commit date), which can only favour them. Because it was trained on uncleaned FX bars (read as near-zero variance), its head is biased low in every year, including its own training years.

## Pre-committed real-time log (strictest test)

Forecasts written to `results/forward/forecast_log.csv` before their outcome existed: 22 core forecasts over 2 target dates (2026-11-02, 2026-11-03). Meridian M0 QLIKE 0.3068 vs frozen HAR 0.3005 (**+2.1%**), Meridian better on 6/11 assets; per date: 2026-11-02 +13.0%, 2026-11-03 -10.4%. These used the previous day's VIX (FRED delay), so they correspond to the real-time-vintage row in the Snapshot A table, not to the same-day row.
